description:
Seven functions Elixir allows in guards have no definition in lib/kernel.fz: abs/1, round/1, trunc/1, floor/1, ceil/1, hd/1, tl/1. They fail the same way in a body and in a guard, because the name does not exist:

- body: dbg(abs(-3)) -> error[lower/unbound]: compiler2 lowering found unresolved direct runtime callee abs/1
- guard: def f(n) when abs(n) > 2 -> error[lower/unbound]: compiler2 guard call abs/1 is unresolved in this namespace
(same for hd/1; probed on fz-rs7.4, PR #358)

They are pure: no allocation, no side effect. Since fz-rs7.4 a guard operator resolves as a call to the Kernel function a body calls, and a guard may call an extern that returns an integer or float or declares raises:. So each is defined once in Kernel and serves both places.

Shape:
- abs/1: integer and float clauses over C externs. abs of the minimum 64-bit integer declares raises: ArithmeticError.
- round/1, trunc/1, floor/1, ceil/1: float -> integer externs declaring raises: ArithmeticError for a float outside the 64-bit range; the integer clause is the identity.
- hd/1, tl/1: a non-empty list answers; anything else raises ArgumentError in a body and fails the clause in a guard. If a guard cannot yet call a Kernel function whose failure is a Fz raise rather than a declared extern failure, that is found here and reported before building.

Fails before, passes after, three paths, with Elixir oracles: each function in a body and in a guard (function head and receive), including the failing argument in a guard choosing the next clause.

Also absent from Kernel and not part of this ticket: max/2, min/2 (not guard functions), bit_size/1, binary_part/3, is_map_key/2.

Acceptance: full gate green.
title: Kernel has abs, round, trunc, floor, ceil, hd and tl, in bodies and guards
